title: A non-pth-power has nonzero differential over a finite coefficient subring
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p$, and $n,m\geq0$. Let $C$ be a domain equipped with a ring isomorphism $C\cong k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $K$ be its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $M/K$ a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of characteristic $p$, with the $C$-algebra structure on $M$ induced through $K$. If $z\in M$ is not a $p$th power in $M$, then there is a subring $A\subset C$ such that $C$ is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $\mathrm dz\ne0$ in $\Omega_{M/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], using the composite $A\hookrightarrow C\to M$.

proof.text: Choose a p-basis (t_i) of k. For finite J construct k_J as the subfield generated by pth powers and the t_i outside J. Construct C_J as the coefficient-supported subring k_J[[x_1^p,...,x_n^p]][y_1^p,...,y_m^p] and K_J as the subfield of fractions of C_J in K. Transport C_J through the given ring isomorphism. The power-series subfields theorem gives finiteness of C over C_J, containment of K^p in K_J, intersection equal to K^p, and the decreasing union-index property.

In M set T_J to the subfield generated by M^p and the image of K_J. The second assertion of the intersection-subfields theorem gives intersection_J T_J=M^p. Each T_J contains M^p and T_(J union Jprime) is contained in both T_J and T_Jprime because taking generated subfields preserves inclusion.

The universal differential of z over F_p is nonzero since z is not a pth power. Apply the first assertion of the intersection-subfields theorem to M and the family T_J. It gives J such that this differential maps to a nonzero element in Omega_(M/T_J).

The image of C_J lies in T_J. Therefore the universal T_J-derivation kills C_J and is a C_J-derivation. Its universal lift Omega_(M/C_J) to Omega_(M/T_J) sends dz to dz. Nonzero dz in the latter makes dz in the former nonzero. Take A=C_J; its finiteness was obtained in the first step.

In a finite extension of the fraction field of a polynomial ring over multivariate power series in characteristic p a non pth power has nonzero differential over a subring over which the polynomial power series ring is module finite

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_subring_nonzero_differential
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type t) [Field k] [CharP k p] (n m : ℕ)
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [IsDomain C]
    (e : C ≃+* MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra C K] [IsFractionRing C K]
    (M : Type w) [Field M] [CharP M p] [Algebra C M]
    [Algebra K M] [IsScalarTower C K M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (z : M) (hz : ¬ ∃ x : M, x ^ p = z) :
    ∃ A : Subring C,
      letI : Algebra A M := ((algebraMap C M).comp A.subtype).toAlgebra
      Module.Finite A C ∧ D A M z ≠ 0
